Looking at the z-index values and stacking context rules:

- `root>low>inner` has `z-index: 999` and `position: absolute`
- `root>high` has `z-index: 2` and `position: absolute`

Both elements are positioned absolutely within the same stacking context (the root element with `position: relative`). When elements overlap in the same stacking context, the one with the higher z-index value appears on top.

Since 999 > 2, `root>low>inner` (the blue box labeled "inner") will be rendered on top of `root>high` (the red box labeled "high") in the overlapping region. This matches the screenshot, where the blue box is visibly on top of the red box.

ANSWER: root>low>inner
